solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Married — be as him changing wife

parts.note: M is the standard abbreviation for married, as on forms and in genealogies

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of the words be as him are being rearranged

explanation.surface: A man is told to swap roles with his wife and behave as she does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' turns BE AS HIM into EMSAHIB, placed after M.
explanation.definitionFit: A memsahib was the title for a married European woman in colonial India, so a wife in that setting.

clue.text: Go wrong with job

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake, to go wrong
and means along with

explanation.surface: Someone makes a mess of a piece of work.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand is a short task or job, such as going to the shops for someone.

clue.text: Great meal, only 1p

indicators.note: only 1p tells us to keep just one P, removing the other from the word for meal

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: A bargain: a terrific dinner costing a single penny.
explanation.walkthrough: '1p' looks like a price, one penny; it means a single letter P.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is an informal word for excellent or great.

clue.text: Without thinking, race around dead trees

indicators.note: around means the race word wraps the other pieces

parts.note: a heat is a qualifying race
D is the abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies
firs are coniferous trees

explanation.surface: Recklessly, runners race around trees that have died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' is a noun here, a heat, not the verb the surface suggests; 'around' makes it wrap the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To rush in headfirst is to act impetuously, without thinking first.

clue.text: Bending pins, say, during game

indicators.note: during means the example abbreviation goes inside the name of the game

parts.note: bowls is a game played on a green, rolling balls at a jack
e.g., for example, is what say means here

explanation.surface: Skittle pins tilt, for instance, in the middle of a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pins' is slang for legs; 'say' gives EG. Bowls is a lawn game popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Bow legs curve outward at the knee, so they are limbs bending; pins is slang for legs.

clue.text: Two secretaries have clearly vacated Vatican office

parts.note: a PA is a personal assistant, a secretary; two of them give the pair
the second of the two personal assistants

indicators.note: vacated means emptied of its contents, leaving only the outside letters of clearly

explanation.surface: Two office secretaries have plainly walked out of their jobs at the Vatican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacated' empties CLEARLY down to its ends, C and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The papacy is the position and authority of the Pope, the highest post in the Vatican.

clue.text: Wine that's very good (I'm joking!)

parts.note: pi is slang for pious, very good in a sanctimonious way
tagging not on a statement says it was a joke, as in great idea... not

explanation.surface: Someone praises a wine, then admits they were only kidding.
explanation.walkthrough: PI is crossword slang for pious; the jokey 'not!' cancels a statement.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinot is a family of grape varieties and the wines made from them, such as Pinot Noir.

clue.text: Get along or get upset through concern for closeness

indicators.note: through means the turned pieces pass inside the word for concern

parts.note: pity is concern or sympathy for someone

indicators.note: get upset means the words before are turned over and read backwards

parts.note: to mix with people is to get along socially
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to rub along with others or else get upset over worries about intimacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get upset' turns the first two pieces backwards together, and 'through' places them inside the concern word after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Proximity is nearness in space or relationship, which is closeness.

clue.text: Battle demands slaughter over retreat

parts.note: a cull is a selective slaughter of animals
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
a den is a private retreat or hideaway

explanation.surface: A war demands killing before any withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: Culloden (1746) was the last pitched battle on British soil, in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Culloden is the 1746 battle in which the Jacobite rising was crushed.

clue.text: Criminal charge after good father shot in Italy?

indicators.note: after places the criminal charge following the letter for good

parts.note: a rap is a criminal charge, as in taking the rap
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A mafia-style tale: a criminal is charged after a good father is shot dead in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' is not gunfire but a small measure of spirit; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Grappa is an Italian brandy usually drunk as a small glass, a shot, after a meal.

clue.text: Demand nothing but in an extravagant way

parts.note: to want something can mean to require or demand it
nothing but means only, as in nothing but trouble

explanation.surface: A spoilt person demands nothing, yet lives lavishly.
explanation.definitionFit: Wantonly can mean lavishly or without restraint, an extravagant manner of acting.

clue.text: In charge

parts.note: read not as being in command but as a charge paid to get in

explanation.walkthrough: 'In charge' looks like being in command; read it as the fee you pay for going in.
explanation.definitionFit: An admission fee is literally a charge for getting in to an event or venue.

clue.text: Stand, fall, and prepare to return

parts.note: to trip is to stumble or fall

indicators.note: to return means the word for prepare is read backwards

parts.note: to do a dish or room is to prepare it

explanation.surface: Instructions: stand up, take a tumble, then get ready to come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand' looks like an instruction but is a noun, the definition; 'to return' reverses the word for prepare.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-legged support for a camera or telescope is a type of stand.

clue.text: Without control, fell after rising

indicators.note: after puts the word for fell following the word for rising

parts.note: a rising or uprising is a time of public unrest
rain fell, so rained can stand for fell from the sky

explanation.surface: Someone lost control and fell after getting up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' is a revolt, not getting up; 'fell' is what rain does.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrestrained describes behaviour not held back or checked, lacking any control.

clue.text: Immature about one being dressed for duty

indicators.note: about means the immature word goes round the letter for one

parts.note: unformed means not fully developed, immature
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A young recruit dressed up for service.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone uniformed wears the official outfit of their job, ready for work.

clue.text: River eroding rocks around head of another river

parts.note: R is the usual map abbreviation for river

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters enclose the first letter of the next word
rocks as a verb means shakes, so the letters of eroding are jumbled
head of picks the first letter of the word another

explanation.surface: A river wearing away rocks near the source of a second river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' turns ERODING into IOGRNDE, and 'around' puts A from 'head of another' inside it; R comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rio Grande is the river forming much of the border between the USA and Mexico.

clue.text: Meet tramp on horse

parts.note: a bum is a vagrant or tramp
a pinto is a piebald horse

explanation.surface: A vagrant riding a horse comes to a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To bump into someone is to meet them by chance.

clue.text: Uncovered area I couldn't nosy around

indicators.note: around signals that the letters of I couldn't nosy are moved about

explanation.surface: A curious visitor complains they could not snoop around an exposed area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges I COULDN'T NOSY, the apostrophe ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: A settlement where people go about unclothed is an area of uncovered bodies, playfully put.

clue.text: Big man associated with Bible law extracts

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing size meaning big
Moses received the commandments, the law of the Bible

explanation.surface: A towering figure tied to scripture's law gives readings from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extracts' as a verb: the process draws liquid through a membrane.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmosis draws liquid through a membrane, so as a verb-like process it extracts fluid; the plural form is a noun.

clue.text: Young doctor in the wrong, oddly

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters of the words the wrong

explanation.surface: A junior medic is in the wrong, strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes T, E, R, N from THE WRONG, after IN.
explanation.definitionFit: An intern is a recent medical graduate working in a hospital under supervision, a junior doctor.

clue.text: Withdraw from work market

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
to tout goods is to market or sell them pushily

explanation.surface: A trader decides to pull out of the labour market.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt out is to choose to withdraw from a scheme or arrangement.

clue.text: Brown edges for somebody's golden buttons

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour

indicators.note: edges for means only the first and last letters of somebody are used

explanation.surface: Brown trim for someone's gold buttons on a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edges for' gives S and Y from SOMEBODY; the 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: Tansy is a plant with flat yellow flower heads like buttons, called golden buttons.

clue.text: Trader planned to fit castle with central heating

indicators.note: to fit means the pieces are fitted inside the word for planned

parts.note: something meant was intended or planned
in chess notation the castle or rook is R
CH is the usual abbreviation for central heating, as in house adverts

explanation.surface: A developer intended to install central heating in a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the two pieces that go in.
explanation.definitionFit: A merchant is someone who buys and sells goods, a trader or dealer.

clue.text: Award collected by the female poet

indicators.note: collected by means the award is gathered inside the word for the female

parts.note: her refers to the female
the OM, the Order of Merit, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A woman poet picks up an award.
explanation.walkthrough: The OM (Order of Merit) is an exclusive British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer was the ancient Greek poet of the Iliad and the Odyssey.

clue.text: Sea creatures writhing on seamen

indicators.note: writhing means twisting about, so the letters of on seamen are jumbled

explanation.surface: Stinging marine animals wriggle over sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea anemones are soft-bodied marine animals with tentacles, so these are sea creatures.

clue.text: Song without so much feeling

definitions.meaning: a musical piece performed in a show is a ...
more numb, having less sensation, the comparative of numb

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading says the word as comparative of numb, a different pronunciation.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece in a musical show is a number; and more numb means having less feeling.

clue.text: Large work, strangely lacking in heart

parts.note: a machine that goes is working

indicators.note: lacking in heart means the central letter is taken out of the word for strangely

parts.note: oddly means strangely

explanation.surface: A big piece of work, oddly without any soul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking in heart' drops the middle D of ODDLY, leaving ODLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodly is an old word for considerable or large in size, as in a goodly sum.

clue.text: Bad language of sport embodied by chant

indicators.note: embodied by means the word for sport is held inside the word for chant

parts.note: to chant is to sing in a repeated tune
to sport clothing is to wear it

explanation.surface: Football crowds' chants are full of foul language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sport' is to wear, as in sporting a hat, not a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Swearing is the use of oaths and obscenities, i.e. foul or bad language.
